title: Army Special Forces graduate first batch of Robotics Technician Integrators, a new job the rest of the service is eyeing
key_facts: Ten warrant officers graduated from the Army’s Robotics Technician Integrator (390A) course at Fort Bragg, North Carolina, on Friday (2 Oct 2026).
It is the first batch of a new military job (MOS) and the end of a pilot inside Army Special Forces (ARSOF); the rest of the Army is eyeing it.
The course lasted 19 weeks: AI skills, coding, and using robotics including drones, unmanned ground vehicles, sensors, electronic warfare and autonomous tools.
Architect Chief Warrant Officer 5 Michael Updike says special operations found a gap in understanding, from brigade level up, on how to integrate robotics into operations.
Graduates will advise commanders at group and brigade level on using robotics in operations and training.
Candidates were screened with a psychological assessment, interviews, packet reviews and a basic coding, software and robotics test.
The pilot stays within ARSOF for now, but Gen. Christopher LaNeve, acting Army chief of staff, said in a press release: "We are scaling this across the Army."
quote_evidence: Ten warrant officers graduated from the Robotics Technician Integrator (390A) course in a ceremony at Fort Bragg, North Carolina on Friday, marking the official start of the new job skill and culmination of an initial pilot program the rest of the Army is eyeing, military officials told DefenseScoop.
While the pilot remains within ARSOF for now, it may scale across the Army, which has “voiced their interest in doing so,” said spokesperson Maj. George Wasickanin.

“These technical experts will help command teams understand integration across the force,” Gen. Christopher LaNeve, the Army’s acting chief of staff, said of the new MOS, according to a press release.
why_it_matters_hint: The Army is creating a dedicated job to turn drone and robot experiments into everyday use.
notes: Full article read. Breaking Defense (see C11-01) says the Army memo expands the 390A job to all applicable Army units, which fits LaNeve’s statement.
